opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__facts:
This is the first bail application filed by applicant under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973, as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.69/2023 registered at Police Station Industrial Area, District Dewas (MP) for offence punishable under Section Sections 354, 354-A, 341,
323, 376(2)(N), 506, and 34 of IPC and Sections 5(L) read with Section 6 and Section 7 read with Section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012.
The applicant is in custody since 10/02/2023.
The allegation against the applicant is of rape of the prosecutrix, aged around 16 years and four months.
Counsel for the applicant has submitted that prior to the present FIR No.69 of 2023, an FIR was lodged by the applicant's side at Crime No.68 of 2023 under Sections 323, 294, 506 and 34 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__decision:
On due consideration of submissions, perusal of the case-diary and the different statements recorded by the prosecutrix, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.
The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

opennyai_summary.final__facts: The appellant has been convicted under Section 363, 366, 376(3), 506(II) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I for 5 years, 5 years, life imprisonment, 1 year, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/-, Rs.1000/-, Rs.2000/-, Rs.500/-, Rs.2000/- with default stipulation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The prosecutrix has remained with the appellant for about 12 days without raising any alarm.
The source of recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register has not been proved.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the case of Tijubai @ Omvati Bai and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2025(1) MPLJ (Cri.)75, it has been held that if the prosecution does not prove the source of date of birth recorded in scholar register and the same is recorded on the guess, the same cannot be the basis for conviction.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the prosecution has failed to prove the source of recording the age of prosecutrix in the scholar register, the judgment passed in the case of Tijubai (supra) and the fact that the age of the appellant was 21 years at the time of incident, we are of the considered opinion that the appellant is entitled for grant of suspension of sentence.
